title: Cum… esset
readingOutcome: Read circumstantial/temporal cum and longer subordinate clauses.

authoringPolicy.method: short concept introduction → authentic example → guided recognition → controlled manipulation → liturgical reading → retrieval
authoringPolicy.vocabularyPolicy: Frozen Lesson 25 connective vocabulary only; complex narrative nouns/proper names are explicit support.
authoringPolicy.authenticTextPolicy: Longer syntax is anchored in Vulgate narrative, Gloria, hymn and traditional liturgical texts.
authoringPolicy.copyrightPolicy: Pedagogical prose and exercises are original synthesis.

sources.sourceLatin: Christi autem generatio sic erat. Cum esset desponsata mater ejus Maria Joseph, antequam convenirent, inventa est in utero habens de Spiritu Sancto.
sources.provenanceNote: cum esset gives the principal imperfect-subjunctive circumstantial frame.

sources.sourceLatin: Cum ergo natus esset Jesus in Bethlehem Juda in diebus Herodis regis, ecce Magi ab oriente venerunt Jerosolymam.
sources.provenanceNote: cum + pluperfect/imperfect-subjunctive narrative frame is read as background circumstance; exact tense formation beyond the lesson is supplied.

sources.sourceLatin: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?
sources.provenanceNote: si introduces a compact condition and retrieves pronoun/preposition syntax.

sources.sourceLatin: Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest introire in regnum Dei.
sources.provenanceNote: nisi introduces an exceptive/negative condition in a doctrinal sentence.

sources.sourceLatin: Quoniam tu solus Sanctus. Tu solus Dominus. Tu solus Altissimus, Jesu Christe.
sources.provenanceNote: quoniam introduces the explanatory/causal conclusion of the Gloria.

sources.sourceLatin: Ubi caritas et amor, Deus ibi est.
sources.provenanceNote: ubi provides a compact locative/conditional-style clause in traditional liturgical song.

sources.sourceLatin: Quando corpus morietur, fac ut animae donetur paradisi gloria.
sources.provenanceNote: quando introduces a future temporal clause linked to a prayer request.

sources.sourceLatin: Dum medium silentium tenerent omnia, et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet, omnipotens sermo tuus, Domine, de caelis a regalibus sedibus venit.
sources.provenanceNote: dum introduces a sustained temporal background with imperfect-subjunctive/indicative narrative texture in liturgical Scripture.

sources.sourceLatin: Nam, etsi ambulavero in medio umbrae mortis, non timebo mala: quoniam tu mecum es.
sources.provenanceNote: nam, etsi and quoniam show layered discourse and conditional/causal relations.
quasi is introduced from the traditional Quasimodo Introit opening.

casePanel.policy: All six cases remain active; Stage 5 closes by requiring case, mood and clause linkage simultaneously across longer passages.

cumClauseFramework.corePattern: cum + imperfect/pluperfect subjunctive often supplies background circumstance in narrative: when/while/since/although, according to context.
cumClauseFramework.imperfectSubjunctiveRecognition: Commonly built from the present infinitive + personal endings: esse → essem/esses/esset..., amare → amarem..., etc.
cumClauseFramework.caution: cum is multifunctional: earlier it was a preposition with ablative; here it is a conjunction introducing a clause. Decide from what follows.

learningBlocks.title: cum can introduce a whole circumstance

learnerCopy.en: You already know cum + ablative as 'with'. Before a finite verb, cum can instead introduce a subordinate clause. With the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive it often supplies narrative background: when, while, since or although.
learnerCopy.fr: Vous connaissez déjà cum + ablatif au sens de « avec ». Devant un verbe conjugué, cum peut introduire une proposition subordonnée. Avec l'imparfait ou le plus-que-parfait du subjonctif, il fournit souvent l'arrière-plan narratif : lorsque, tandis que, puisque ou bien que.

fr.title: cum peut introduire toute une circonstance

learnerCopy.en: The imperfect subjunctive is highly recognizable because it is built on the present infinitive: esse → esset, amare → amaret, venire → veniret. In cum esset, the infinitive-shaped stem is the clue.
learnerCopy.fr: L'imparfait du subjonctif est très reconnaissable car il se construit sur l'infinitif présent : esse → esset, amare → amaret, venire → veniret. Dans cum esset, la base d'infinitif est le signal.

learnerCopy.en: The cum-clause establishes the circumstance before the main event inventa est. Do not translate word by word first; mark the subordinate boundary and find the main verb.
learnerCopy.fr: La proposition en cum établit la circonstance avant l'événement principal inventa est. Ne traduisez pas d'abord mot à mot : marquez la limite de la subordonnée et trouvez le verbe principal.

learnerCopy.en: si introduces an open condition; nisi normally means 'unless / if not'. These clauses may use different moods depending on meaning, so the conjunction identifies the relation, not a fixed mood by itself.
learnerCopy.fr: si introduit une condition ; nisi signifie normalement « à moins que / si... ne ». Ces propositions peuvent employer différents modes selon le sens : la conjonction indique la relation, non un mode fixe à elle seule.

fr.title: si et nisi encadrent les conditions

learnerCopy.en: quando, dum and ubi locate events; quoniam and nam explain; atque/ac, vero, etiam and quidem connect or shade discourse. These small words are what make long prayer and narrative passages navigable.
learnerCopy.fr: quando, dum et ubi situent les événements ; quoniam et nam expliquent ; atque/ac, vero, etiam et quidem relient ou nuancent le discours. Ces petits mots rendent les longs passages de prière et de récit navigables.

learningBlocks.title: Stage 5: hold several clauses at once

learnerCopy.en: The Stage 5 gate requires multi-clause reading: identify main and subordinate clauses, recognize subjunctive mood, distinguish purpose/result/condition/time/cause, and keep case/pronoun resolution active across the whole passage.
learnerCopy.fr: Le contrôle de l'étape 5 exige une lecture à plusieurs propositions : distinguer principale et subordonnées, reconnaître le subjonctif, différencier but/résultat/condition/temps/cause et maintenir l'analyse des cas et pronoms sur tout le passage.

fr.title: Étape 5 : tenir plusieurs propositions à la fois

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Christi autem generatio sic erat. Cum esset desponsata mater ejus Maria Joseph, antequam convenirent, inventa est in utero habens de Spiritu Sancto.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Christi autem generatio sic erat. Cum esset desponsata mater ejus Maria Joseph, antequam convenirent, inventa est in utero habens de Spiritu Sancto.

translation.en: Now the generation of Christ was in this wise. When His mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child, of the Holy Ghost.
translation.fr: Voici comment arriva la naissance du Christ. Marie, sa mère, étant fiancée à Joseph, avant qu'ils eussent habité ensemble, se trouva enceinte par l'Esprit-Saint.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Cum ergo natus esset Jesus in Bethlehem Juda in diebus Herodis regis, ecce Magi ab oriente venerunt Jerosolymam.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Cum ergo natus esset Jesus in Bethlehem Juda in diebus Herodis regis, ecce Magi ab oriente venerunt Jerosolymam.

translation.en: When Jesus therefore was born in Bethlehem of Juda in the days of King Herod, behold there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem.
translation.fr: Jésus étant né à Bethléem de Judée, au temps du roi Hérode, voici que des Mages vinrent d'Orient à Jérusalem.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?

translation.en: If God be for us, who is against us?
translation.fr: Si Dieu est pour nous, qui sera contre nous ?

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest introire in regnum Dei.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto, non potest introire in regnum Dei.

translation.en: Unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
translation.fr: À moins de renaître de l'eau et de l'Esprit-Saint, nul ne peut entrer dans le royaume de Dieu.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Quoniam tu solus Sanctus. Tu solus Dominus. Tu solus Altissimus, Jesu Christe.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Quoniam tu solus Sanctus. Tu solus Dominus. Tu solus Altissimus, Jesu Christe.

translation.en: For Thou only art holy. Thou only art the Lord. Thou only art most high, O Jesus Christ.
translation.fr: Car vous seul êtes Saint. Vous seul êtes Seigneur. Vous seul êtes le Très-Haut, Jésus-Christ.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Ubi caritas et amor, Deus ibi est.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Ubi caritas et amor, Deus ibi est.

translation.en: Where charity and love are, there is God.
translation.fr: Là où sont la charité et l'amour, Dieu est présent.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Quando corpus morietur, fac ut animae donetur paradisi gloria.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Quando corpus morietur, fac ut animae donetur paradisi gloria.

translation.en: When my body shall die, grant that to my soul be given the glory of paradise.
translation.fr: Quand mon corps mourra, faites que soit donnée à mon âme la gloire du paradis.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Dum medium silentium tenerent omnia, et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet, omnipotens sermo tuus, Domine, de caelis a regalibus sedibus venit.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Dum medium silentium tenerent omnia, et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet, omnipotens sermo tuus, Domine, de caelis a regalibus sedibus venit.

translation.en: While all things were in quiet silence, and the night was in the midst of her course, Thy almighty Word, O Lord, came down from heaven from the royal throne.
translation.fr: Alors qu'un profond silence enveloppait toutes choses et que la nuit était au milieu de sa course, votre Verbe tout-puissant, Seigneur, vint du ciel, du trône royal.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Nam, etsi ambulavero in medio umbrae mortis, non timebo mala: quoniam tu mecum es.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Nam, etsi ambulavero in medio umbrae mortis, non timebo mala: quoniam tu mecum es.

translation.en: For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils: for Thou art with me.
translation.fr: Car, même si je marche au milieu de l'ombre de la mort, je ne craindrai aucun mal, parce que vous êtes avec moi.

Distinguer cum préposition de cum conjonction.
